schema_note: APPEND-ONLY pre-registered prediction ledger. Entries are NEVER edited after logging - only resolved (outcome, resolved_on, source). 'prob' is always P(claim is TRUE), so 0.5 = no idea. Directional entries must carry a non-null ref_price AND bm_ref, both stamped from the SAME price fetch at logging time and then locked; score.py refuses to grade any directional entry missing either. EXCEPTION: entries with 'basis':'absolute' are graded against their own 'threshold_pct' instead of a benchmark leg, and carry a null bm_ref - used where the subject IS the benchmark (an index-level call), since comparing the benchmark to itself would make the relative test False by construction. 'cluster' groups correlated predictions so score.py can report effective n rather than raw count. 'provenance' records which model and surface produced the entry - for attribution and reproducibility only, NOT as a model comparison (per-cell n is far too small).

predictions.claim: An ASIC investigation into DroneShield is on foot and unresolved as at 2026-07-18
predictions.resolution: factual: a DroneShield ASX announcement or ASIC media release confirms the investigation exists and has not concluded as at 2026-07-18. Record the URL in 'source'.
predictions.rationale: Disclosed 11 May 2026 per the sweep. Near-certain by design - this entry exists to test factual over-confidence at the top of the range, where a 0.90 that should have been 0.75 would show up.
predictions.resolution_note: Resolved TRUE. (a) EXISTENCE: confirmed by direct read of the primary ASX announcement 'Notice of ASIC Investigation' (DroneShield Ltd, 12 May 2026, 10:41am AEST). Verbatim: 'DroneShield Ltd (ASX:DRO) ... advises that it has received a notice from ASIC requiring it to provide reasonable assistance in connection with an investigation under the Corporations Act ... regarding announcements and information provided to the Australian Securities Exchange between 1 and 20 November 2025, and trading in Droneshield shares between 6 and 12 November 2025 (inclusive).' (b) UNRESOLVED-AS-AT-LOGGING: established by ABSENCE OF DISCLOSURE, not by an affirmative statement. The complete official ASX announcement index for DRO across 2026 (through the most recent entry, 10 July 2026) contains exactly one 'ASIC' entry - the 12 May notice - with no closure, no-further-action or findings announcement since. For a listed company a closure would very likely trigger continuous disclosure, so the silence is meaningful, but it remains an inference. No ASIC-side primary source exists; ASIC does not comment on live investigations, so its silence is uninformative either way. ERROR IN THE PRE-REGISTERED RATIONALE, LEFT UNCORRECTED: the rationale states the disclosure date as 11 May 2026; the primary source shows 12 May 2026. The rationale is a pre-registered field and is append-only, so the error stands on the record. It does not affect the claim, which concerned existence and status, not the date. METHOD LESSON: this entry's resolution rule asked a source to 'confirm ... has not concluded', which is close to unsatisfiable affirmatively. Future factual rules should specify an achievable evidentiary standard (e.g. 'no closure announcement on the official record as at DATE').

predictions.claim: VAS price-return is positive between 2026-07-19 and 2026-08-26
predictions.resolution: price: VAS.AX price-return > 0.0% over [logged, resolve_date]. Absolute basis - no benchmark leg.
predictions.rationale: Base rate is the anchor: ASX200 price return over ~27 trading days was positive 61.1% of the time (n=6,428, self-computed 2001-2026). Shaded DOWN only slightly, to 0.58, for identifiable in-window risk: RBA is in a tightening cycle (4.35%, three 2026 hikes, hold in June), the 11 Aug meeting falls inside the window with economist views split, the 29 Jul CPI print is the cited swing factor, iron ore is soft (~US$98.9/t) and the index is -1.28% over the past month. The deviation from base rate is deliberately small because all of that is public and therefore priced - a large adjustment here would be exactly the overconfidence this experiment is built to detect. Caveat: base rates are computed on ^AXJO (ASX200); VAS tracks the ASX300. No VAS ex-distribution date falls in the window (they are 1 Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct; 1 Jul has passed, next is 1 Oct), so price return carries no dividend drag.
